messages.subject: Re: Using Distance data outside distance
parts:
Dear colleagues,

Has anyone tried to use R data created by Distance DSM analysis module
outside Distance (directly using R MGCV library)?
In the R workspace I easily found all the predictor variables in the
sample.dat.101 data object. However, I am not able to find the data of the
response variable. I expected to find it in the obs.dat.101 data object.
There are 4 variables in that table: object, distance, size and
Sample.Label. However, the variable "size" contain only values "1". So it
cannot be the right response variable.
The command that Distance sends to R suggests that response variable could
be named 'group.est'. However, I cannot find a variable under this name in
any of the data objects related to this (101) analysis.
> > dsm.101<-
> > dsm.fit(ddfobject=ddf.79,response='group.est',model.defn=list(fn='gam',family='quasipoisson'),wghts=NULL,off=covered,link='log',formula=~te(x.coord,
> > y.coord) + s(depth, k=4)+ s(depth.var, k=4) + s(di.coast, k=4) +
> > s(di.bedrock, k=4) + s(di.mixed, k=4) + s(di.muddy, k=4) + s(di.sandy,
> > k=4) + s(di.silt,
> > k=4),obsdata=obs.dat.101,segdata=sample.dat.101,convert.units=1)
Or should I look into ddf.79 or any other data object of analysis 79 (the
MRDS analysis which is used in the DSM fit analysis)?
I did not find any documentation on the structure/contents of the data
objects created by Distance in the html files provided with DSM and MRDS
libraries.
I would greatly appreciate any hint on where to look for the response
variable of the DSM fit analysis?

best wishes
Ainars Aunins

messages.author: 12f269733c6eb9a2
messages.subject: Re: Using Distance data outside distance
parts:
Ainars:

The question you ask is a bit complicated, and unfortunately so is the
answer. The short answer to 'where is the response variable' is that
the response variable is created within the dsm.fit() function. The
longer answer deals with what response variable is selected by you, and
how should that be created.

I will explain the most common case; you (the analyst) wishes to
estimate the number of individuals in the population, and the sightings
are of groups (clusters) of animals. So in this case the response
variable is the number of individuals in each segment of your transect.
So how is the number of individuals in each segment computed (it is
after all an estimate because detectability is imperfect and needs to be
estimated, hence the number of individuals in each segment is estimated).

The estimation of number of individuals per segment is derived using a
Horwitz-Thompson type estimator with the numerator being the size of
each cluster detected in a segment, and that number being divided by the
probability of detection for that cluster. If there is more than one
cluster detected in a segment, the adjusted count is summed over all
detected clusters.

That is how the calculation of the response variable is performed, but
you asked where do those values reside in the R workspace. The values
themselves do not reside in an R object, but the constituents needed for
the calculation do exist within the "ddf" objected created by mrds()
during the fitting of the detection function. Note the ddfobject is the
first argument passes to the dsm.fit() function. Specific to the code
snippet you provided, if you interrogate "ddf.79" you will find the bits
used by dsm.fit() to create the response variable. Within the ddf
object resides the sizes of the clusters as well as the detection
probabilities associated with each cluster. With this information,
dsm.fit() is able to create the response variable for further modelling.

I appreciate that the documentation on this topic is thin. Let me know
if this answers your question and how I can make the explanation clearer.

messages.author: 350dad0a615d36db
messages.subject: Re: Using Distance data outside distance
parts:
Ainars, list,

The response can be found in the fitted dsm object (dsm.101 in your example, below). The "result" element holds the result of the call to gam(), so looking in dsm.101$result$data should reveal the data frame that was used to fit the model, the response is names N in all cases. The model can then be refitted in mgcv, should you wish. To ensure that you have the same model as was fitted in Distance you may want to interrogate elements like $call, $formula and $family. the ?gamObject manual page may also be useful. (Note that saving the data is not the default behaviour for gam().)

As Eric noted, the response has a different interpretation depending on what you specified the response to be, so refitting the exactly the same model is possible, or the same model with smooths of different variables. The response will change if, for example, the covariates are changed in the detection function.

On a related note, I am currently finishing a new dsm package that will make analyses within R much easier. There will be a post to this list when the release is ready.

All the best,
--dave
